output.name: Rathun
output.myth: Rathun was a ketch out of the western harbour, and she went to sea the week Tavo came down laughing. The gale took her stern and stove it in like a bad crate. Her crew bailed with their hats, then their boots, then their bare hands, and when the water stood at their knees they sang the old net-song so Tavo would hear something new. Tavo did not stop, but he grew curious, the way Aun always did. He lifted the ketch on his shoulder, carried her over the Leeward rocks, and set her down in the Upper Sea where the wind runs clean. She lies a fist north-west of the Oilskin Coat, so the rain that runs off Mot's coat falls on her open stern. Her sails are full, though the wind goes in one side and out the other. Sil sees her on dark nights and waves. Eighteen degrees south, in the Unflown, the Kite for the Drowned Child keeps her company. Old sailors say that if you hold your breath off the Unflown, you may still hear her bailing.
output.finding: From the Oilskin Coat, which hangs low in the Leeward Reach, look one fist north-west, about 10°, and you will find the Holed Ketch.
